calls.head: Best against best
calls.body: The Kings are near the top of the league for shot volume, and the Panthers are one of the league’s best at keeping shots away. We think the Panthers win this one.
calls.call: The Panthers keep the Kings under the league-average 56.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Los Angeles 7th for shot volume (60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Florida 2nd for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, Los Angeles had 41.6 per 60. The league average is 56.9 per 60, and they came in at 60.3 per 60.

calls.head: Bruisers against finesse
calls.body: On physicality, Florida is the league’s best and Los Angeles is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Panthers hit more than the Kings in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Florida had hit score 190 and Los Angeles hit score 77. Coming in, Florida was at hit score 144 and Los Angeles at hit score 88.
calls.usual: FLA hit score 144 · LAK hit score 88
calls.tonight: FLA hit score 190 · LAK hit score 77
calls.beyond: Florida’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 190, against their usual 144 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

LAK.head: We had this close to even (50% for Los Angeles), and it went Florida’s way.

FLA.head: We had this close to even (50% for Florida), and Florida came through.

surprises.head: Florida couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Florida’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Los Angeles shortened their bench
surprises.body: Los Angeles’s bottom-six forwards played 37% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 9 games.

story.head: The Panthers beat the Kings
paras: Alex Laferriere opened the scoring late in the first. Matthew Tkachuk scored the winner midway through the third.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: The Kings haven’t won in three.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
